definitions.explanation: The historical background or pedigree of a place, family, or thing, especially when it is long, distinguished, or noteworthy. Most commonly encountered in the compound 由緒ある (having a distinguished history).

examples.japanese: {由緒|ゆいしょ}ある{神社|じんじゃ}を{訪|おとず}れた。
examples.english: I visited a shrine with a distinguished history.

examples.japanese: この{旅館|りょかん}は{由緒|ゆいしょ}{正|ただ}しい{建物|たてもの}で、{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}から{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: This inn is a building with a distinguished pedigree, having been in operation since the Edo period.

examples.japanese: この{刀|かたな}には{由緒|ゆいしょ}があり、かつてある{有名|ゆうめい}な{武将|ぶしょう}が{所有|しょゆう}していたと{伝|つた}えられている。
examples.english: This sword has a notable history, and it is said to have once been owned by a famous military commander.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used in the set expressions {由緒|ゆいしょ}ある (having a distinguished history) and {由緒|ゆいしょ}{正|ただ}しい (of distinguished/legitimate lineage). Typically describes temples, shrines, families, inns, and historical objects.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {由緒|ゆいしょ}ある (having a distinguished history)
- {由緒|ゆいしょ}{正|ただ}しい (of impeccable lineage, prestigious)
- {由緒|ゆいしょ}ある{寺院|じいん} (temple with a distinguished history)
- {由緒|ゆいしょ}を{誇|ほこ}る (boast a distinguished history)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歴史|れきし}: history (general, broader meaning)
- {伝統|でんとう}: tradition (customs passed down, not specifically lineage)
- {来歴|らいれき}: history, provenance (the story of how something came to be)
